# Frozen KMutexDelete implementation handoff

User now explicitly authorizes implement for this reviewed KMutexDelete experiment. Freeze predicate `kmutexdelete-predicate-r1` and spec `S2-19632ed3e5482b4086f38e90555d504a40f14a9eb89a23fc04ccf5d377ad4271`. See `.docs/Report/predicate-review.md`, `spec-review.md`, `source-consistency.md`, and `.docs/checks/shared-migration.json`. Live predicate is `/home/xinra/crtos/lib/KMutexDelete.v`, hash 7a4fe9106548d5f07aca0fa278e182b37535b9d346654e7c4d30ae041da63d50. All shared predicate semantics and every caller-local/canonical contract are frozen. Shared files and the four reused-spec files are read-only during per-case owner work; do not silently change their meaning or add assumptions.

Three implementation targets (separate controller cases): LinklistResumeAll (mutex_waiters_oc), _MutexDelete (assumed_environment), KMutexDelete (assumed_environment). Preserve the original three critical-section boundaries and all executable C behavior. Do not apply proposed source fixes. Reused-spec boundaries: IdGetObj, IdRemoveObj.low_level_spec, DoubleLinkListRmNode.remove_member, KTaskWakeup.wakeup_by_id_ic; sources/hashes are in `.docs/Report/reused-spec-imports.md`. Do not generate implementation VCs or reprove their bodies. Other new target contracts are modular callee boundaries whose own implementation runs must also complete before overall success.

TrustBase: `/home/xinra/TrustBase.md`, readonly. Existing CriticalAreaLock/UnLock, allocator x_free via KERNEL_FREE, and CONTAINER_OF model contracts retain their listed scope. User additionally approved A1: same allocation survives from successful lookup through this removal (no other delete/free/reuse); A2: no new waiter joins after drain until removal. These are explicit caller-scoped environment restrictions. mutex_live/mutex_drained lock contracts and guarded observation programs implement exactly these restrictions; do not turn them into ordinary global lock guarantees, freeze unrelated state, add axioms, or assume a pending proof obligation as a fact. Original defects remain in unrestricted executions.

OS annotation adaptation: may add/fix by local, where instantiations, branch-control, Inv/multi-inv, and which-implies annotations. These must retain every real path, ownership and generated proof obligation. C bodies are single-function slices; spec stage intentionally did not supply complete invariants/ghost inference. Add/prove function-specific auxiliary lemmas in each allowed case lib, directly importing the real shared definitions; no Admitted/Parameter/Axiom or placeholder definitions. If frozen spec/predicate needs semantic change, produce concrete proposed delta and stop for main/user review; do not unfreeze yourself.

Keep existing trial annotated_C, _CoqProject, external mappings and global library namespace. QCP tool-side project_layout adapter supports this trial with qcp-project.json (32-bit little-endian no-CRules GCC); VC output uses KMutexDeleteProof.VC. Do not copy shared dependency trees or change to QCP_examples layout. Toolchain is `/home/xinra/crtos/tools/rocq/toolchain.json`, same exact Coq core as prior successful interactive checks. Use required Rocq MCP interaction for proofs; batch compile does not replace it. Main drives all controller actions until done or explicit blocker.

Formal *_obligation definitions are unproved proposition statements. In particular, prove required drain loop/aggregate bridge and retirement resource transformations; never use those definitions as theorem evidence. Case-specific helpers must leave reviewed source semantics unchanged. Original source/config unchanged since design, so source consistency review remains applicable unless body/config is changed.
